proposedTopics.title: Web3 / Solidity / DeFi
proposedTopics.description: A long-term, depth-first Web3 path: fundamentals, Solidity, tooling, standards, gas, security, DeFi, EVM internals, frontier and full-stack. Authored chapter order is a study preference; prerequisite edges name the concepts actually needed. Keep every strand, study one primary leaf deeply, and bring forward a small tool or application lesson when your current lab or project needs it.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Path root, created 2026-07-07; concept-gate revision 2026-09-25. Preserve depth-first study and the complete long-term catalogue. Begin with the Ethereum operating model and a minimal Foundry bootstrap (Foundry project anatomy; cast and anvil as needed), then deepen tooling during contract work. Raw Ethereum JSON-RPC and viem can support the read-only wallet early. Study DeFi numerical models before their advanced attacks; security basics accompany the first contract. Phase numbers express authored order, not universal gates or deadlines. Record compiler/library/chain versions for each lab. Keep one primary topic and one project milestone active; larger Build tasks belong to practice sessions, with short recall and later independent changed-case checks.

proposedTopics.title: Phase 1 — Blockchain & Ethereum Fundamentals
proposedTopics.description: How Ethereum works: accounts, transactions, gas, the EVM, PoS consensus, L2s/rollups, account abstraction, and the 2025–26 protocol state (Pectra/Fusaka). Mostly theory; entry point.

proposedTopics.title: Phase 2 — Solidity Language
proposedTopics.description: The Solidity language end to end: types, storage, functions, inheritance, events, errors, low-level calls, ABI, signatures, assembly intro.

proposedTopics.title: Phase 3 — Tooling: Foundry & Hardhat
proposedTopics.description: Bootstrap Foundry project anatomy early for local labs; deepen testing, fuzzing, invariants and deployment as the contract exercises need them. Hardhat 3 is an alternative TS toolchain, not gated by finishing all Foundry lessons.

proposedTopics.title: Phase 4 — Core Contract Patterns & Standards
proposedTopics.description: Token standards (ERC-20/721/1155/4626), proxies/upgradeability, access control, signatures/permit/meta-tx, airdrops, multisig, factories, DAOs — each with its threat model.

proposedTopics.title: Phase 5 — Gas Optimization
proposedTopics.description: Exhaustive gas: storage packing, warm/cold access, calldata, unchecked, bitmaps, custom errors, assembly, architecture.

proposedTopics.title: Phase 6 — Security & Auditing
proposedTopics.description: The full attack taxonomy + audit methodology, static analysis, fuzzing/invariants, report writing, wargames (Ethernaut, Damn Vulnerable DeFi v4), real-exploit replays, and CodeHawks First Flights.

proposedTopics.title: Phase 7 — DeFi Mechanics & From-Scratch Builds
proposedTopics.description: Build DeFi from scratch: AMMs, Uniswap V2→V3→V4, lending, stablecoins, oracles, staking/restaking, perps, vaults, flash loans.

proposedTopics.title: Phase 8 — EVM Internals & Advanced Solidity
proposedTopics.description: Opcodes, Yul/Huff, storage/memory/calldata at the bytecode level, proxies at bytecode level, formal verification.

proposedTopics.title: Phase 9 — Frontier Strands
proposedTopics.description: MEV, intents/ERC-7683, Uniswap V4 hooks, restaking, RWAs, ZK and L2 internals. Choose each strand when its actual concept prerequisites are ready; unrelated strands remain independent.

proposedTopics.title: Phase 10 — Full-Stack dApp
proposedTopics.description: Public RPC, viem/wagmi, wallet lifecycle, contract reads/writes and indexing. Begin read-only wallet work after the RPC/account basics; deepen ABI, signing and contract behavior as those milestones need them.
